conviction_note: abs_move 6.0 (event-implied 5.71 on an illiquid chain, own median 5.81, a fresh Q2 outlook comes with the print) times a 54% up probability. The lean is small: consensus sits inside the company's own Q1 guide, and HB Fuller's quarter covering the same months showed pricing ahead of raw costs. Against that, Brent went back above $100 in September, which threatens the H2 raw-material assumption behind the FY27 guide, and the put skew agrees with that. The two measurements roughly agree: findings sum +0.3 against +0.48 scaled.
bar: Q1 FY27 adj EPS $1.95 (+3.7% y/y vs $1.88) and revenue $2.22bn (+4.9-5.2%), with the EPS consensus down 0.5% over 30 days (Zacks via Yahoo, 2026-10-01: https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/exploring-analyst-estimates-rpm-international-121502287.html ; Investing.com preview 2026-10-05: https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/rpm-international-earnings-in-focus-as-construction-slows-93CH-4932363). Segment consensus: Consumer $717.7m (+3.4%), CPG $939.4m (+6.6%), PCG $559.6m (+3.9%). Company Q1 guide (2026-07-22 call): mid-single-digit sales growth and mid-single-digit adj EBITDA growth, raw material inflation 5-6%, $25m of SG&A savings (https://www.rpminc.com/media/qffpsp3a/rpm-4q26-earnings-transcript.pdf). FY27 guide: sales +3-7%, adj EBITDA +5-10%. The two estimate sources agree, and the consensus sits at or slightly below the guide midpoint.
positioning_check: Short interest 3.28m shares, 2.61% of float, 2.04 days to cover, down from 3.67m the month before (stockanalysis.com, read 2026-10-05 by the sweep; the FINRA settlement date is not shown: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/rpm/statistics/). Not a crowded short. Skew is +10.48 vol points (25d put IV minus call IV), so downside is being paid for, but the chain is thin: total OI 385 and an ATM spread of 57% of mid. The skew is weak evidence. The stock is -6.2% over 20 sessions on the baseline (Investing.com says about -15% over a month), -17.7% from its 52-week high and +6.1% off the low. Sell-side is still Buy-heavy (14 of 15 Buy per Investing.com) while targets drift down: Morgan Stanley $117->$114 EW on 2026-09-28, Wells Fargo $135->$130 OW on 2026-10-05.

findings.finding: H.B. Fuller, a direct adhesives/sealants peer whose fiscal Q3 (to 2026-08-29) covers almost exactly RPM's Q1 (Jun-Aug), reported on 2026-09-23: pricing +7.4% more than offset a 3.0% volume decline, Building Adhesive Solutions +5.2% organic, adj EBITDA +9% with margin +80bp to a record 19.9%, adjusted gross margin +120bp, and it RAISED its FY2026 guide (adj EBITDA $655-670m, EPS $4.70-4.85). RPM guided Q1 price/cost as 'somewhat negative', with gross margin pressure from 5-6% raw inflation. A peer showing price ahead of raws in the same months points to RPM's gross margin landing at or above its own cautious framing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: RPM trades on the quarter's EPS surprise: +12.4% on 2026-04-08 (adj EPS $0.57 vs $0.35, margin-driven) and +5.8% on 2026-07-22 ($1.89 vs $1.83). The Q2 FY26 miss on margins/demand drew a negative reaction (baseline 2025-04-08 -9.1% was a prior miss).
findings.why_not_priced: RPM consensus EPS was trimmed 0.5% over the last 30 days and the stock fell about 15% in the month, so analysts did not mark RPM's Q1 margin up after Fuller's print. If the peer read-through had been priced, Q1 estimates would have moved toward the top of the mid-single-digit EBITDA guide rather than down.
findings.independence: Sherwin-Williams Q2 (July) also beat, raised guidance and announced an 8% price increase effective 2026-09-01, showing the coatings chain passing inflation through (https://seekingalpha.com/news/4580909-sherwin-williams-keeps-2026-guidance-unchanged-while-raising-raw-material-inflation-outlook). It is a different document and an earlier quarter. Proxy: Fuller's raw-material basket differs from RPM's (RPM is more exposed to PO/MDI and solvents).

findings.finding: Brent crude went back above $100 in September and early October 2026: $101.21 on 09-09, $104.82 on 09-17, near $108 intraday on 09-28, $102.31 on 10-01. It had been $88-93 through August and ~$72-78 in late June/early July. On 2026-07-22 RPM framed the FY27 guide (+5-10% adj EBITDA) as assuming 'current raw material costs remain stable', with inflation moderating in H2, and already guided Q2 raw inflation to as high as 6-8%. The Q2 outlook given with the print, and any comment on the FY guide, now has to absorb higher petrochemical inputs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On 2025-10-01 (Q1 FY26, a record quarter with a cautious outlook) the stock moved -0.59%. The negative reactions in the baseline (-9.1% on 2025-04-08) came with margin and outlook pressure. On the July call the CEO called the H2 raw-material assumption 'a swag'.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: RPM fell about 15% in the month the oil spike happened, Sherwin-Williams also sits ~15% off its high, and the put skew is bid. What is not priced is whether management cuts the FY27 EBITDA range or only widens the H2 caveat. A cut would show as a gap below the low end; a hold would remove the overhang.
findings.independence: Al Jazeera 2026-09-28 on Brent nearing $108 (https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2026/9/28/oil-prices-surge-after-trump-rejects-irans-plan-to-reopen-strait-of-hormuz). Company transmission comes from RPM's own July transcript (https://www.rpminc.com/media/qffpsp3a/rpm-4q26-earnings-transcript.pdf). This is macro-to-company transmission, and the cost hit lands with a FIFO lag, mostly in Q2-Q3 rather than in the reported Q1.

findings.finding: Consensus Q1 EPS of $1.95 (+3.7% y/y) and revenue of $2.22bn (+4.9%) sit at or slightly below the company's own Q1 guide: mid-single-digit sales growth, mid-single-digit adj EBITDA growth, $25m of incremental SG&A savings, and buybacks stepped up to $25m+/quarter with $815m authorized. The EPS consensus was cut 0.5% in the last 30 days. RPM has beaten EPS on its last two prints ($0.57 vs $0.35; $1.89 vs $1.83).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS beats were bought: +12.4% (2026-04-08) and +5.8% (2026-07-22). The tough-comp October print (2025-10-01, record $1.88) drew -0.59%.
findings.why_not_priced: The bar sits inside the guide, so an in-line-to-modest beat is what the market was told to expect. That is why this finding is small. If a beat were not already the base case, the consensus would sit above the guide midpoint rather than below it.
findings.independence: Company guide from the July transcript (https://www.rpminc.com/media/qffpsp3a/rpm-4q26-earnings-transcript.pdf). The second estimate source, Investing.com (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/rpm-international-earnings-in-focus-as-construction-slows-93CH-4932363), agrees on $1.95/$2.22bn.

findings.finding: The DIY channel in RPM's quarter was mixed but not worse. Home Depot Q2 (to 2026-08-02) comps were +1.7% against +0.9% expected, with paint among 13 of 16 positive departments, though Pro outpaced DIY. Lowe's Q2 (to 2026-07-31) comps were +0.2% with paint positive, but it cut FY sales to the bottom of its range on persistent DIY pressure. RPM's Consumer segment (consensus $717.7m, +3.4%, helped by acquisitions) was guided to 'stabilization' after unit volume of -2 to -3% in Q4.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Consumer weakness was named in the Q2 FY26 miss (late Oct/Nov DIY softening). Consumer is about 32% of sales, so a consumer miss has been offset by CPG/PCG in recent prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Small and mostly public. If retail paint/DIY strength were priced into RPM Consumer, its segment consensus would sit above the acquisition-aided +3.4%. Net of the rest of the company: CPG/PCG (~68% of sales) carry the print, so this moves the total little.
findings.independence: Lowe's Q2 release (https://www.nasdaq.com/press-release/lowes-reports-second-quarter-2026-sales-and-earnings-results-2026-08-19) points the other way on DIY and the same way on paint. Proxy: RPM's Rust-Oleum/DAP mix is not interior paint.

findings.finding: Non-residential construction stayed soft through RPM's quarter. The AIA/Deltek ABI was 47.2 in August (46.6 in July), inquiries were only modestly up, newly signed design contracts declined, and the share of firms expecting declines rose to 29%. Carlisle (Q2, 2026-08-07) put reroofing at +3% and commercial new construction down mid-single digits. RPM CPG consensus is +6.6% and PCG +3.9%, and RPM itself said 'underlying commercial construction continues to be weak' and that 95% of Tremco Roofing is restoration/reroofing.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: CPG/PCG beats drove the last two positive prints (+12.4%, +5.8%). Construction slowdown commentary preceded the Q2 FY26 miss.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The Investing.com preview leads with 'construction slows', and RPM guided assuming weak new construction. The open question is only whether CPG's acquisition- and price-aided +6.6% consensus is too high.
findings.independence: Carlisle Q2 2026 call (https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2026/08/07/carlisle-csl-q2-2026-earnings-call-transcript/). It is a direct roofing peer and shows reroofing resilient, which partly offsets the ABI read.

findings.finding: RPM flagged on 2026-07-22 that a fire at a primary chemical supplier (LyondellBasell's Bayport propylene-oxide unit, force majeure after the 2026-03-12 fire) would hit Tremco Roofing Q1 costs and 'some negative impact on sales growth', with relief expected by the end of summer. It also flagged tight MDI supply.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior instance of this line in the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside the guide: the company told the market and the guide includes it. It is only worth anything if the disruption ran past August and spills into the Q2 outlook.
findings.independence: ChemAnalyst 2026-06-02 on Bayport force majeure easing and PO prices declining 3% in late May (https://www.chemanalyst.com/NewsAndDeals/NewsDetails/us-propylene-oxide-prices-decline-3-07-as-softer-feedstock-42581) suggests the supply side was normalizing.

findings.finding: Buyback capacity against a weaker price. In July the board added $700m to the remaining $115m authorization, and the CEO said RPM would be 'opportunistic in the event of weakness in our stock price'. The stock was ~$117 on 2026-08-05 and is $98.95 now, about 15% lower. The Q1 10-Q/release will show the pace, and the call may signal acceleration.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2026-07-22 +5.8% reaction came with the record Q4 and the $700m buyback increase together.
findings.why_not_priced: The authorization is known. An explicit accelerated repurchase after a 15% drawdown would be news, and the absence of any 8-K since July means nothing has been announced.
findings.independence: The CEO Form 4 of 2026-08-05 records an option exercise and a sale at $116.72, establishing the price level (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000110621/000119312526340385/ownership.xml).

findings.finding: CEO Frank Sullivan exercised 200,000 options at $62.17 on 2026-08-05, sold 106,529 shares at $116.72 (~$12.4m) and withheld 40,753 for tax/exercise, keeping 1,065,995 shares directly. Sales came near the subsequent high.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public and routine (an option exercise with a partial sale), so it is close to nothing. Filed for completeness.

findings.finding: RPM closed the acquisition of Volteco, an Italian below-grade waterproofing maker with ~€28m of 2025 sales, into Tremco CPG on 2026-10-01. That is about 0.3% of RPM sales, with terms undisclosed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Bolt-on M&A has not moved the stock on prints.
findings.independence: Investing.com preview names it as a monitoring point (https://www.investing.com/news/earnings/rpm-international-earnings-in-focus-as-construction-slows-93CH-4932363).

baseline_tension: The small long lean cuts against the +10.5-point put skew, but the chain is thin (OI 385, 57% spread). The September oil re-spike that the skew and the 15% one-month drawdown appear to price is filed as the main negative, so the lean rests on the reported quarter (consensus inside the guide, a peer showing price ahead of raws) while the guide risk is acknowledged.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (inside the guide): the consensus-vs-guide finding moved from +0.6 to +0.3 because the bar sits inside what the company guided; the supplier-fire finding moved from -0.2 to -0.1 because it was already guided.

Lesson 5 (proxy): HB Fuller read-through trimmed from +0.8 to +0.7 as a peer proxy, but kept substantial because 'a peer's print landing after the company last spoke' is the pattern that has paid. Consumer DIY proxy trimmed +0.3 to +0.2 (lesson 9: net of the 68% of the company outside Consumer).

Lesson 7 (skew): the oil/guidance negative agrees with the skew and the drawdown, so it is partly priced; trimmed from -1.0 to -0.8. p_up moved from 55 to 54 because the long lean runs against the (thin) skew.
Construction ABI trimmed from -0.3 to -0.2 because the direct roofing peer (Carlisle) shows reroofing resilient. Buyback trimmed from +0.4 to +0.3. Volteco set from +0.1 to 0.0 as immaterial.
The Investor Day 2026-11-09 remained outside_window in both drafts.
